answer: A bonded identity registry makes each agent lock a refundable stake before it can trade. Creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand stakes, so attack cost scales linearly. Like timber braced at a single vertex, the registry holds only while every joint is funded: a gale of new aliases from one wallet stands out in the funding graph, and a caught fake forfeits its stake, so Sybils pay more than they can ever earn back.
